--- title: "Introduction to APIs" --- ## What is an API? API stands for **application programming interface**. An API gives software a standard way to ask another service for data or an action. For example, a researcher can send a gene symbol to an API and receive gene information in a format that Python can read. This is faster and easier to repeat than copying results from a website by hand. ## Parts of an API request | Term | Meaning | |---|---| | Endpoint | The web address used for a specific task | | Request | The message sent to the API | | Parameter | A value that controls the request, such as a gene or tissue ID | | Response | The information returned by the API | | JSON | A common text format used to organize returned data | An API request should record the endpoint, parameters, resource version, and date. These details help another person repeat the request. ## Common biomedical APIs | API | Example use | |---|---| | [NCBI E-utilities](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/home/develop/api/) | Search and retrieve records from NCBI resources such as Gene, PubMed, and Protein | | [Ensembl REST API](https://rest.ensembl.org/) | Retrieve genes, variants, sequences, and comparative genomics data | | [UCSC Genome Browser API](https://genome.ucsc.edu/goldenpath/help/api.html) | Retrieve genome sequences and selected annotation tracks | APIs work best for focused requests. Large datasets are often better downloaded as complete files. ## APIs used in this module | CFDE resource | API role in this module | |---|---| | [GTEx Portal API](https://gtexportal.org/api/v2/docs) | Request median gene expression for named tissues | | [HuBMAP APIs](https://docs.hubmapconsortium.org/apis.html) | Find cells, datasets, metadata, and atlas information | | [Pharos GraphQL API](https://pharos.nih.gov/api) | Request selected fields about human protein targets | ClinVar can also be accessed through NCBI E-utilities. The variant table in this module uses saved ClinVar-linked annotations. ## REST and GraphQL REST APIs usually provide a set of endpoints for different tasks. GTEx, HuBMAP, Ensembl, and UCSC provide REST-style access. GraphQL uses one query endpoint. The request names the exact fields it needs. Pharos uses GraphQL in this module. ::: {.optional-activity} ## Optional Website Activity: Build an API request This code builds an NCBI Gene search URL without sending the request. Change `MYH7` to another gene symbol and choose **Run Code**. ```{pyodide} from urllib.parse import urlencode endpoint = "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi" parameters = { "db": "gene", "term": "MYH7[gene] AND Homo sapiens[organism]", "retmode": "json", } request_url = f"{endpoint}?{urlencode(parameters)}" request_url ``` ::: ::: {.knowledge-check data-answer="The web address used for a specific task" data-correct="An endpoint is the address used for one API task." data-incorrect="Review the API terms table above."}
